text:
maria: heads-up — hitting flaky SSE parse errors in the Node SDK during reconnects. Repro in our sample app: sometimes the stream stops parsing JSON until the connection times out, then on reconnect we get duplicate tokens.

aj: can you paste a minimal repro and the raw SSE frames?

maria: pasted logs below — you can see the server sends:

id: 42
data: {"chunk":"hello"}

then a few seconds later the proxy forwards `data: {"chunk":" world"}` but the client receives it as `data: {"chunk":"hello"}\ndata: {"chunk":" world"}` in one TCP chunk with only a single blank line at the very end. Node's parser seems to buffer until the double-CRLF, which is fine, but when we abort the request mid-chunk and reconnect with `Last-Event-ID: 42` the server resends the event with id 42 and we end up applying the same token twice.

sam: interesting — Python eventsource client we use tolerates single-newline boundaries and also dedups by `id` automatically. Node's eventsource-ish parser behavior might differ. Are both SDKs exposing the raw `id` header?

leo: quick notes from infra: some proxies (haproxy/nginx) will re-chunk or coalesce SSE frames when buffering is enabled for keepalive. Also TLS record boundaries are not preserved so chunking is unreliable. You should never rely on TCP chunk boundaries for SSE.

maria: agreed, but two problems here: (1) Node parser waits for blank line and blocks longer than our client SLOs, causing timeouts; (2) reconnect + Last-Event-ID semantics are causing duplicates if the server resends the last event and the SDK does not deduplicate by `id` before emitting tokens.

aj: can you share the minimal client snippet you used?

maria: here's the Node snippet to reproduce (curl also repros):

```js
const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Accept: 'text/event-stream' } });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while (true) {
  const { done, value } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  process.stdout.write(value); // raw bytes show merged events
}
```

And this is the server SSE sequence we used (explicit ids):

```
id: 42
data: {"tok":"A"}

id: 43
data: {"tok":"B"}

```

If you force a reconnect after token A but before token B arrives the server may resend id 42. Node client ends up emitting A again.

leo: reproduction idea — run nginx with `proxy_buffering on` and a tiny flush interval; that reliably reproduces coalesced frames. Also add a client abort in the middle.

infra-bot: noticed 0.8% spike in stream reconnects for sample-app on staging at 2026-03-18T14:22:10Z :warning:

sam: for SDK parity we should do two things: (a) make Node and Go dedupe by `id` on reconnect prior to delivering data to user callbacks, (b) make parser accept multiple newline styles and deliver partial events faster (configurable small timeout flush).

aj: agree. Also add an integration test that runs against haproxy/nginx that intentionally coalesces and splits events mid-json to catch regressions. Add a small sample app flow in docs that shows `Last-Event-ID` behavior and how to opt into `dedupe: true` if users want it.

maria: workaround today is to have server-side idempotency on tokens or include an incremental `seq` field in the JSON and dedupe at app layer. But SDK-level dedupe would remove a lot of friction.

leo: implementation notes: dedupe by `id` is cheap (keep last N ids in ring buffer); for long-lived streams we should garbage collect. Also add a `sse.strictNewline = false` toggle so users can choose to be tolerant.

aj: action items:
- aj: file an SDK GH issue for Node + Go dedupe + parser timeout (PR welcome with tests)
- sam: add integration test harness with nginx/haproxy and sample-app (use docker compose)
- maria: add a short reproducible sample in `examples/streaming-resume` and a note in docs about `Last-Event-ID` semantics
- leo: check whether any prod configs have buffering enabled for our hosted routers and add observability around `Last-Event-ID` duplicates

maria: thanks — I'll open the sample app PR now and link the logs here. :thumbsup:

dev-bot: deploy queued for staging: sample-app-streaming-fix branch (CI running)

aj: once PRs are up let's also add a small E2E that simulates abort/reconnect and asserts no duplicate tokens are delivered. That should be part of SDK CI.

maria: sounds good — I put the minimal nginx repro and a `curl` script in the PR so reviewers can run locally.

sam: nice, this should also fix the onboarding flakiness folks saw where the quickstart stream sometimes hung on the first token.

leo: and we'll also add a short note in the docs: "If you use middleboxes (nginx/haproxy) enable immediate flush for SSE or prefer `dedupe` in the SDK."

maria: filing links: https://git.internal/repo/issue/1234 and PR https://git.internal/repo/pulls/4567 — put comments there if you want to review the test harness.
